summary: Frontend-only parity testing for the ToolWalkthroughVideo rollout across 6 AI tools + statement-decoder regression on both web and mobile (Expo web preview). All 7 web pages and all 7 mobile screens render the walkthrough section with correct test IDs ('<slug>-how-to-video' and '<slug>-how-to-video-player', plus 'sd-how-to-video*' for Statement Decoder), 'Watch the walkthrough' label, correct title + blurb, and a 16:9 player. On web, both the logged-out/blocked branch and the authenticated/allowed branch (verified by code grep AND an in-browser login as cathy@example.com -> /app) show the video — code shows exactly 3 occurrences per web tool page (1 import + blocked branch + allowed branch). Statement Decoder regression passes on both surfaces. No new console errors introduced by this change.
critical_code_review_comments: Pre-existing (unrelated to this change) React hydration warning observed in dev-mode on /ai-tools/care-plan-reviewer: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' at CarePlanReviewer.jsx:582. Appears to be caused by the x-source-file inspector injecting <span> inside <option> elements of a <select>. Not a regression from this iteration but worth cleaning up — only visible under the editor's dev overlay.

ToolWalkthroughVideo.jsx uses preload='metadata' + controls — good. No autoplay. 16:9 letterboxing via aspect-video + contain is correctly applied. Mobile uses expo-video useVideoPlayer with contentFit='contain' — matches the chosen player style and avoids expo-av (deprecated).

Mobile component (ToolWalkthroughVideo.tsx) calls useVideoPlayer(v ? v.url : null, ...) UNCONDITIONALLY before the 'if (!v) return null' early return — this is actually correct for rules-of-hooks (hook order is stable since v either exists or not for the lifetime of that slug), but passing null source to useVideoPlayer may trigger a warning depending on expo-video version. Consider: const player = useVideoPlayer(v?.url || '', ...). Non-blocking.
